## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**System Name:** Main House
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a CRITICAL pump deficiency that requires immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This condition poses a risk of motor damage from overheating without fluid cooling. All other components are in good condition and the dispersal field is dry with no surface breakout.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The liquid level is at the outlet. The effluent filter is in good condition with light soiling and was cleaned and reseated during this visit.

## PUMP ASSESSMENT
| Parameter | Measured | Nameplate | Load % | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amp Draw | 1.6 A | 7.2 A | 22.2% | CRITICAL |

The pump is running but drawing only 1.6 amps against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps. This indicates the pump is operating with no hydraulic load. Possible causes include a dry-running condition (no fluid at the pump inlet), a broken or missing impeller, or a severed or disconnected discharge line. The high water alarm tested functional and electrical connections are sound.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface is dry with no ponding or breakout observed during the field walk.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**CRITICAL -- Immediate professional attention required:**
- The effluent pump is operating with no hydraulic load (22.2% FLA). Inspect the pump inlet for blockage or loss of suction. Verify the discharge line is intact and connected. If the pump has been running dry, the motor is at risk of thermal damage. Do not continue operating the system until the pump load is restored and the cause is identified.

**Routine:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump issue is resolved.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### The Pump Problem
Your effluent pump is running, but it is not moving water. When a pump motor runs without fluid to cool it, the motor windings overheat and can fail. This is a safety issue and needs to be fixed right away.

The most common causes are a clogged inlet screen, a broken impeller inside the pump, or a disconnected or cracked discharge pipe. A qualified technician will need to inspect the pump and its connections to find out which one it is.

### Tank Solids
Your tank solids are at 22.9 percent of tank volume, which is normal and healthy. You are not approaching a pumping threshold. Continue to keep non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, and medications all slow down the biological processes that break down waste.
